title: Cap. X Ultimum Propos. 1.I cont.: Pelagius then grants internal illuminating and exciting grace by persuasion — still not healing the will
pass_a_gloss: Pelagius therefore acknowledged internal grace also: First, illuminating and opening the eyes of the mind. Clear are those words of his in Augustine, De grat. Christi cap. 7. God helps us by his doctrine and revelation, while he opens the eyes of our heart, while he illuminates us with the manifold and ineffable gift of heavenly grace. Secondly, he grants an internal grace exciting the affections, and striving to shake off the will’s torpor, by means of the foresaid illumination, and by a certain secret preceding persuasion. Unto this look those words, Ibid. cap. 10. He works in us to will what is good, while he kindles us, given over to earthly desires, by the greatness of future glory and the promise of rewards; while by revelation of wisdom he raises the astonished will unto desire of God; while he persuades us of everything that is good. Unto this point Pelagius himself was brought.
pass_b_english: So Pelagius also granted internal grace—first illuminating, opening the mind’s eyes. His words in Augustine (De gratia Christi 7) are clear: God helps us by his teaching and revelation when he opens our heart’s eyes and lights us with heaven’s manifold, unspeakable gift. Second, he grants an internal grace that stirs the affections and tries to shake torpor from the will, by that illumination and by a prior secret persuasion. So ibid. 10: He works in us to will the good when he kindles us, given to earthly desires, with future glory’s greatness and the promise of rewards; when by wisdom’s revelation he raises the stunned will to desire God; when he persuades us of all that is good. That far Pelagius himself was led.
source_text: Agnovit igitur Pelagius et gratiam internam: Primo, illuminantem et aperientem oculos mentis. Clara sunt illa verba ejus apud Augustinum, De grat. Christi cap. 7. Adjuvat nos Deus per doctrinam et revelationem suam, dum cordis nostri oculos aperit, dum nos multiformi et ineffabili dono gratiae caelestis illuminat. Secundo, concedit gratiam internam excitantem affectus, et excutere conantem voluntati torporem suum, mediante illuminatione praedicta, et antecedente suasione quadam arcana. Huc spectant illa, Ibid. cap. 10. Operatur in nobis velle quod bonum est, dum nos terrenis cupiditatibus deditos futurae gloriae magnitudine et praemiorum pollicitatione accendit; dum revelatione sapientiae in desiderium Dei stupentem suscitat voluntatem; dum nobis suadet omne quod bonum est. Huc usque perductus est ipse Pelagius.
